summary: Structured-output JSON mode causing sporadic token-decoding stalls and client timeouts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart is seeing sporadic per-request stalls when using the Structured Output (JSON) mode. Requests look like they begin streaming tokens but the stream / HTTP response sometimes hangs for 10-60s at the end of generation and eventually hits client-side timeout. This behavior started after a traffic increase and after the model catalog rolled a minor model variant update last week.

Impact:
- High 95th/99th latency for calls with structured_output=true for this customer
- Several timed-out user-facing requests reported by BrightCart; conversion impact reported by customer CS team
- Occasional increased error rates (up to 2.3% 5xx and client timeouts) for affected routes

Environment:
- Redwood hosted Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated GPU cluster) in us-east-1
- Serving runtime v1.9.2 on dedicated nodes; api-gateway v2.1.0
- Customer requests use structured_output=true and streaming=true with a JSON schema for product_catalog responses

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) POST to /v1/generate with model=open-lama-13b-v2 and structured_output=true
2) Provide schema with nested arrays (catalog -> items[]) and ask for generation with max_tokens ~1024
3) Observe streaming SSE; in ~85% of requests the stream completes normally, in ~15% the stream outputs the closing bracket then stalls (no FIN or stream end) for 15-60s and client disconnects

Observed behavior:
- Token stream appears to emit final content but the HTTP connection remains open without a final stream termination event (SSE end)
- Server-side request remains in RUNNING state on runtime for additional 20-40s after last token emitted
- CPU on the worker spikes during the stall window and then drops when the request finally exits

Expected behavior:
- Stream should close promptly after generation completes and response should be marked as completed with < 2s of post-generation cleanup

Logs / snippets (customer and runtime):
- Customer trace: request_id=cust-BR-7721-20260312
- Runtime worker logs (excerpt):
  [2026-03-12T15:03:10Z] INFO request=cust-BR-7721 token_emit=last_chunk
  [2026-03-12T15:03:10Z] DEBUG json_validator: starting schema finalization
  [2026-03-12T15:03:10Z] DEBUG json_validator: validating 3 nested arrays
  [2026-03-12T15:03:25Z] WARN request=cust-BR-7721 decode_wait: waiting for downstream drain
  [2026-03-12T15:03:48Z] ERROR request=cust-BR-7721 worker=worker-7 hang_detected: blocking syscall in validator

Additional context:
- Customer reports flaky reproduction; not all requests with the same payload hang
- Quick mitigation (customer): disabling structured_output (returning plain text) stops the stalls
- No recent changes to the customer schema; model variant rollout occurred ~72 hours prior to first reports

Attachments:
- Customer's example prompt and schema (sanitized) attached to the ticket
comments: 2026-03-12 16:10 - Asha Patel (Support): Acknowledged. Logged P1 and engaged SRE. Asked customer for sample request/response and request_id. Provided temporary workaround: set structured_output=false or turn off streaming.

2026-03-12 17:02 - Marcus Li (SRE): Looking at worker-7. Saw a user-space validator thread blocking on a regex/utf8 decode syscall during finalization. Adding tracing for blocking syscalls. Asked infra to capture perf record for that worker when it occurs.

2026-03-12 18:40 - BrightCart (Customer CS - Emily Wong): Shared sanitized prompt + schema and noted that issue correlates with lists of >150 items in 'items' array. They can repro internally ~30% of the time with the shared payload.

2026-03-13 09:12 - Marcus Li (SRE): Reproduced locally with stress harness using customer's schema and large arrays. Hypothesis: strict JSON validator path uses a Python-level routine that copies large buffer and performs expensive multi-byte checks which leads to blocking GC/IO under high concurrency.

2026-03-13 11:30 - Eng (runtime) - Sofia Alvarez: Investigating change in model variant that increased average token length in final chunks which triggers validator to re-scan the full response for schema anchoring. Opened PR to add streaming-validation short-circuit for final chunk when schema already satisfied (runtime PR #438).

2026-03-13 14:05 - Asha Patel (Support): Notified customer of investigation and recommended two workarounds: (1) switch to structured_output=false for high-throughput endpoints, or (2) set streaming=false so validation occurs synchronously but avoids streaming race. Customer opted to set streaming=false for critical paths.

2026-03-14 08:50 - Marcus Li (SRE): Deployed tracing agent to dedicated pool for a 2-hour window to capture additional hang traces. Found several stack traces showing 'json_validator.finalize()' holding the GIL and calling regex on 300KB blobs.
investigation_notes: Perf traces show blocking in python json_validator for ~10-30s in affected requests.
Reproduction successful with customer's sanitized schema + large item arrays under load (concurrency 20+).
Kernel-level profiling did not show syscall-level stalls; CPU bound on Python thread (GIL) and expensive string ops are primary suspect.
Model variant change increased average token length and introduced extra trailing whitespace tokens in final chunk; triggers validator to do full-buffer rescans instead of incremental checks.
Temporary mitigation validated: disabling structured_output eliminates the hang; switching to non-streaming also avoids the streaming-end hang.
Related tickets: SUP-7021 (schema validation regressions) and SUP-6012 (stream serialization backpressure) — share similar themes but different root causes.
Proposed permanent fix: implement streaming short-circuit in runtime validator and move heavy validation off the GIL-bound path (native C extension or offload to worker threadpool).
workaround: Customer workaround (accepted): set streaming=false for critical endpoints, which causes validation to be synchronous but avoids streamed hang behavior.
Alternative: set structured_output=false to return plain text and perform JSON parsing client-side.
Throttle concurrent structured-output requests (reduce concurrency below 10) as a temporary operational mitigation.
If using schema with very large arrays, consider paginating items or returning compressed/condensed representations to reduce validation work.
next_steps: Eng (runtime) to merge PR #438 to add streaming-validation short-circuit and run internal perf tests (target: 2026-03-16).
If PR proves effective, schedule hotfix rollout to dedicated pools in us-east-1 (canary then full) — target window 2026-03-17.
Explore implementing C-based validator or offload path to avoid GIL-bound stalls in high-concurrency scenarios (RFC by 2026-03-20).
Postmortem and customer-facing RCA to be drafted after root cause and fixes are deployed; owner: Marcus Li.
resolution: In Progress - runtime PR opened to short-circuit streaming validation (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/438).
Customer accepted workaround and applied streaming=false for critical endpoints; reported immediate reduction in timeouts.
Waiting on performance validation and canary rollout results before marking Resolved.
